summary: A user clicked a link in an email with classic credential-phishing traits: urgent mailbox-suspension wording, a login page on a verify-style domain, and an SPF failure. The click is confirmed, but the alert does not show whether credentials were entered. Treat the account as potentially compromised until that is checked.

evidence.why: The sending server is not authorized for the sender domain, which suggests spoofing or a malicious sender.

evidence.value: Your mailbox will be suspended today
evidence.why: Urgency and a threat of account suspension are typical credential-phishing social engineering.
A login page on a verify-style lookalike domain is consistent with a credential-harvesting page.
A generic support address on the same domain as the phishing URL is not a trusted internal or vendor sender.
The user visited the link, so exposure is confirmed. This does not prove credentials were submitted, which is the main unknown and the only mitigating gap in the evidence.

recommended_action.detail: Reset the user's password and revoke active sessions and tokens now as a precaution. Check proxy and web logs for a POST to account-verify.example.com to see whether credentials were submitted. Review the user's recent sign-ins and mailbox rules for suspicious activity. Block the domain and purge the email from other mailboxes.
